Let \(p=101\). We count how many pairs \((k,j)\), with \(1\le j\le p-1\), give a particular floor value.

For \(n\ge 1\), define

\[
C_n=\#\{(k,j):k\ge 1,\ 1\le j\le p-1,\ \lfloor pk/j\rfloor=n\}.
\]

Then by Tonelli/Fubini,

\[
S=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} C_n 2^{-n}.
\]

For fixed \(j\),

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{pk}{j}\right\rfloor=n
\iff
\frac{nj}{p}\le k<\frac{(n+1)j}{p}.
\]

The interval has length \(j/p<1\), so it contains at most one integer \(k\).

Write \(n=pq+a\) with \(0\le a\le p-1\).

- If \(a=0\), then \(nj/p=qj\) is an integer and lies in the interval, so every \(j\) contributes. Thus \(C_n=p-1=100\).

- If \(a>0\), let \(t\equiv aj\pmod p\) be the least positive residue. Then the interval is

\[
\left[\left\lfloor \frac{nj}{p}\right\rfloor+\frac{t}{p},
\left\lfloor \frac{nj}{p}\right\rfloor+\frac{t}{p}+\frac{j}{p}\right),
\]

so it contains an integer iff \(t+j>p\). Therefore

\[
C_n=\#\{j\in\{1,\dots,p-1\}:(aj\bmod p)+j>p\}.
\]

Now for \(a=p-1=100\), \((aj\bmod p)=p-j\), so \((aj\bmod p)+j=p\), never \(>p\). Hence \(C_n=0\) when \(n\equiv 100\pmod{101}\).

For \(1\le a\le p-2\), let \(r_j\equiv aj\pmod p\). Since \(a\neq p-1\), \(r_j+j\neq p\), so

\[
\mathbf 1_{r_j+j>p}
=
\left\lfloor \frac{r_j+j}{p}\right\rfloor
=
\left\lfloor \frac{(a+1)j}{p}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor \frac{aj}{p}\right\rfloor.
\]

Using the standard identity

\[
\sum_{j=1}^{p-1}\left\lfloor \frac{cj}{p}\right\rfloor
=
\frac{(c-1)(p-1)}2
\qquad (1\le c\le p-1),
\]

we get

\[
C_n
=
\sum_{j=1}^{p-1}
\left(
\left\lfloor \frac{(a+1)j}{p}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor \frac{aj}{p}\right\rfloor
\right)
=
\frac{a(p-1)}2-\frac{(a-1)(p-1)}2
=
\frac{p-1}{2}.
\]

For \(p=101\), this is \(50\). Thus

\[
C_n=
\begin{cases}
100, & n\equiv 0\pmod{101},\\
50, & n\equiv 1,2,\dots,99\pmod{101},\\
0, & n\equiv 100\pmod{101}.
\end{cases}
\]

So the first period \(n=1,\dots,101\) contributes

\[
50\sum_{n=1}^{99}2^{-n}+100\cdot 2^{-101}.
\]

Since the coefficients are periodic with period \(101\),

\[
S=
\frac{50\sum_{n=1}^{99}2^{-n}+100\cdot 2^{-101}}
{1-2^{-101}}.
\]

Now

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{99}2^{-n}=1-2^{-99},
\]

so

\[
S=
\frac{50(1-2^{-99})+100\cdot 2^{-101}}
{1-2^{-101}}
=
\frac{50(2^{101}-4)+100}{2^{101}-1}
=
\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}}
\]
